To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ZnO thin films implanted with phosphorus (P) or with antimony (S) are p-type conductors, despite the doping ion.
the electrical and optical properties are improved by doping and the electrical properties are improved by increasing the dose.

the ZnO:P and Sb-doped films have a p-type conduction with electric resistivity values of 0,012 (omega cm), and 0,042 (omega cm), respectively, and the Raman scattering spectra confirm the polycrystaline nature of the films.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrical and Raman scattering characterization of ZnO thin film produced by r.f magnetron sputter and doped with phosphorus and antimony by ion implantation.
the production of p-type ZnO films, with the aim to use them in optoelectronics applications.
the study of the structural, optical and electrical properties of ZnO films doped with P or Sb.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in spite of the different nature of the dopants (P and Sb), the electrical conductivity of the doped films seems to be mainly governed by the same mechanism: the formation of oxygen vacancies.
ZnO is an interesting semiconductor for p-type conduction and that the doping process can be successfully performed with P and Sb ions by ion implantation.

, in spite of the differences between both dopants, the results obtained for ZnO: Sb films are very similar to those obtained for ZnO:P films, indicating that the doping mechanism is similar for both cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in spite of the fact that ZnO is a wide-band gap semiconductor, its p-type conduction can be obtained by implantation.

the ZnO thin films are p-type semiconductors with electrical resistivities in the range of the semiconducting materials and that the electrical resistivities are lower than those obtained for ZnO doped with other elements, like Al, In or Ga.
the ZnO:P thin films are better for optoelectronic devices than the ZnO:Sb ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the doping with P and Sb is not enough to produce n-type conductivity in ZnO films produced by r. f. magnetron spttering, even when the films are annealed at high temperature (500 degrees C).
, in the case of ZnO:Sb films, the annealing process is essential for obtaining p-type conductivity.
ZnO:P thin films have a higher carrier concentration, mobility, conductivity, and optical transmittance than ZnO:Sb.
